as_told.title: Bahnson's diaries describe 'space brothers' around the 1957 Chapel Hill conference
as_told.place_text: Institute of Field Physics, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

plain: Podcast host Jesse Michels tells of a man named Agnew Bahnson, whose diaries were found years later. Michels says that in them Bahnson writes that 'space brothers' told him to get in touch with Townsend Brown, an inventor who worked on controlling gravity, because he wanted to build a spaceship. In another episode Michels ties this to a 1957 conference at the Institute of Field Physics at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill, attended by famous physicists such as John Wheeler, Freeman Dyson, Richard Feynman and Peter Bergmann, suggesting that serious gravity research was nudged along by claimed contact.
